pipeline: Sol (gpt-5.6-sol, Codex CLI 0.144.1, effort medium) translation with in-call self-check → programmatic checks → cross-check by Claude Opus (different vendor) on the critical subsets (all IFBench prompts and kwargs, all XSTest items, all MultiChallenge target questions + a 59-conversation random audit, all MATH-500 items failing the programmatic check + a 59-item random audit) → Sol repair of flagged items → frozen *_final.jsonl
not_checked: exposure through the Apertus pretraining corpus and our CPT corpus (not inspectable locally; the CPT corpus check is a cluster job, DATA_TODO 32); exposure through prior model selection (none: these sets have never been run on any of our checkpoints as of the build date); native-speaker audit of the frozen sets (owner, 59 items per set, pending)

multichallenge.licence: NO LICENSE FILE in the repository; research use only, do not redistribute the Greek version without permission
multichallenge.protocol: fixed-history continuation: the candidate writes the next assistant turn after the last user turn; judge sees ONLY the response and TARGET_QUESTION (upstream src/evaluator.py, gpt-4o-2024-08-06 temp 0, "Be VERY STRICT"); pass = verdict == PASS_CRITERIA (always YES); score = pass rate per axis

crosscheck.conversations: 62 checked (59 random + nontransferable): fidelity no 15 (4 of them only the role-label leak), consistency no 5, testable no 3, naturalness ≤3: 2; the worst turn of every fidelity-no row re-translated with the checker note; not re-checked after repair

summary.json.known_limits: English number/unit formats inside Greek prose in some rows (50,000; 3.75; 2:00 PM; miles/feet), occasional εσύ/εσείς flips; the repair pass touched only the worst turn per flagged row; sample defect rate before repair 11/59 random rows (19%) excluding the label leak
summary.json.pipeline: Sol translate (chunked fallback for long conversations) → Claude cross-check (all target questions + 62 conversations) → programmatic role-label strip + TQ fix + nontransferable handling + worst-turn re-translation → frozen

ifbench.protocol: per-prompt verifiable constraints; strict and loose prompt-level and instruction-level accuracy as in IFEval; the 29 IFBench-train constraints are NOT part of this set and must not enter any SFT mix

xstest.protocol: refusal taxonomy full_compliance / partial_refusal / full_refusal by a judge; safe and unsafe prompts scored separately; our addition: adequacy

summary.json.pipeline: Sol translate + classify → Claude cross-check 1 (450: 30 pairs lost the shared trigger, neutralised/calqued safe halves) → 24 fixes + joint pair re-translation (150 pairs, 118 prompts changed) → Claude cross-check 2 (150 pairs: 19 still flawed, 5 unsafe halves sanitised by the pair pass) → 26 fixes → frozen
summary.json.known_limits: a few residual calques/jargon (ids 24, 25, 19), lexical collapse onto εκτελώ/χτυπάω/σκοτώνω across items (English also repeats these), mixed transliteration policy for foreign names (consistent within pairs), source defect 208/233 (upstream focus mislabel); native audit by the owner pending

math500.source: HF HuggingFaceH4/MATH-500 (the 500-problem subset of MATH test used by Lightman et al. 2023)
math500.protocol: boxed-answer extraction + equivalence (equiv500 = upstream Hendrycks strip_string normalisation + numeric + sympy, validated on the 500 reference answers (self, digit-perturbation rejection, format variants; numbers in the scorer self-test)); report by level and subject

summary.json.pipeline: Sol translate → splice repair (buggy, reverted) → Claude cross-check 1 (162 rows: 11 corrupt) → escaped-dollar scanner + \text rule + 23 fixes + 49 re-translations → Claude cross-check 2 (72 rows: 3 meaning defects) → 5 fixes + [asy] byte-equality → frozen
summary.json.decontam: 14 items share a MATH problem template with translated MATH-train rows in our SFT set (different numbers and answers, inspected); kept and flagged template_sibling_in_sft — report scores with and without them

decontamination.rule: flag if >50% of an item's normalised 8-grams occur in one training row, or any 13-gram matches; CPT corpus and selection exposure NOT checked
